title: Agnelli: The Rules of the Game
description: The Agnelli dynasty, Fiat, power, wealth and the captivating world of Italy's most glamorous industrial family.

title: La Vita Agnelli
description: Gianni Agnelli's remarkable life, his family, his influence and the extraordinary world he inhabited.

title: The Gentleman Icon: Porfirio Rubirosa
description: The Dominican diplomat and legendary international playboy at the heart of the mid-century jet set.

title: The Good Life Aquatic
description: Aristotle Onassis's yacht Christina O and the fascinating guests and intrigues of its glamorous heyday.

title: Lady Diana Cooper — Forty Years Since Her Death
description: The dazzling society figure, wit and diplomat's wife whose circle included Churchill, Cecil Beaton and Evelyn Waugh.

title: The Legend of Rubirosa
description: A spirited, richly sourced long profile that reconstructs the life of Porfirio Rubirosa — polo player, diplomat, racing driver and legendary jet‑set lover — weaving scandal, Trujillo’s politics and Rubi’s celebrity into a vivid portrait of mid‑century high society. The piece captures both his glamorous conquests and the darker ties to Dominican power with anecdote‑driven narrative and archival reporting.

title: Potemkin Playboys
description: A polished, elegiac essay on the passing of Gunter Sachs and the end of a particular European playboy era, mixing biography, social history and stylish reportage to examine Sachs’s marriages, art ambitions and his role as a mid‑century icon of leisure and taste. The piece is narrative‑forward and rich in atmosphere, situating Sachs among the jet‑set circuits of St. Moritz, Saint‑Tropez and Gstaad.

title: A Delicate Balance
description: A long, textured look at Aristotle Onassis’s private life and public marriages that balances his business empire, famed romances (including Maria Callas and Jacqueline Kennedy) and the personal dramas that shaped his legacy; the piece draws on memoirs and contemporary reporting to render Onassis as both a titan of shipping and an architect of modern high society mythology. It’s narrative‑rich and attentive to character detail and historical context.

title: The Legend of Peter Beard
description: Photographer, Kenyan wilderness adventurer and notorious society wild man: an extraordinary life spent between African game trails and New York's most glamorous parties.
subject: Peter Beard

title: Robert Capa's Longest Day
description: The swaggering, romantic war photographer lands at Omaha Beach on D-Day, producing eleven surviving photographs and one of journalism's most extraordinary stories.
subject: Robert Capa

title: The Last Queen of Paris
description: The mysterious French countess at the heart of postwar high society recalls outrageous masked balls, Diana Vreeland, Cecil Beaton and a lifetime of immaculate reinvention.
subject: Jacqueline de Ribes

title: A Short, Bumpy Ride with Steve McQueen
description: A vintage encounter with Hollywood's king of cool, capturing the combustible star in the middle of his sixties fame rather than looking back from a safe distance.
subject: Steve McQueen

title: The Wild Life and Many Loves of Ava Gardner
description: A fiercely independent movie star with legendary allure, tempestuous romances and a gift for turning the most improbable evenings into Hollywood folklore.
subject: Ava Gardner

title: Mad, Bad, and Dangerous to Know: The Mythical Life of Errol Flynn
description: A rakish screen legend who made his own life almost as wildly improbable as his swashbuckling films, leaving a trail of scandal and self-mythology.
subject: Errol Flynn

title: All That Glittered
description: Inside the extravagant life of the Mexican-born host whose legendary 1951 Venice costume ball helped define a vanished world of European society.
subject: Charles de Beistegui

title: Bye Society
description: Truman Capote charms his way into the confidence of New York's most dazzling women, then loses the world he craved by putting its secrets into print.
subject: Truman Capote

title: Homicide at Rough Point
description: At a Newport mansion, one of America's richest and most formidable heiresses becomes embroiled in a death that refuses to fade from society's memory.
subject: Doris Duke

title: The Lost City of Z
description: David Grann's investigation into the disappearance of British explorer Percy Fawcett and his search for a fabled Amazonian city called 'Z.' A gripping mix of archive-driven detective reporting, atmospheric jungle scenes and a portrait of deadly obsession in the era of empire—the piece later grew into Grann’s book The Lost City of Z.
subject: Percy Fawcett / Amazon exploration / lost-city mystery

title: The Shipwreck Detective
description: Sam Knight profiles enthusiasts and professionals who hunt for historic shipwrecks using modern technology. The story combines forensic maritime history, vivid salvage scenes and the strange, almost romantic obsession with sunken vessels—an elegiac look at loss, treasure and the people who chase it.
subject: shipwreck hunting / maritime archaeology

title: The Shipwrecks From John Franklin’s Doomed Arctic Expedition Were Exactly Where the Inuit Said They Would Be
description: In 1845 two Royal Navy ships vanished into the Arctic with 129 men. An absorbing investigation of their doomed search for the Northwest Passage, and the eyewitness accounts that eventually helped solve the mystery.
subject: Franklin expedition

title: Why a Minnesota Man Walked Around the World, Traversing 13 Countries and 14,450 Miles in Four Years
description: Two brothers walked out of their Minnesota hometown on a wildly ambitious round-the-world expedition. The journey took them through palaces, deserts and mortal danger—and only one would make it home.
subject: David Kunst

title: Who Was Casanova?
description: The Venetian gambler, fugitive and self-invented charmer covered Europe by stagecoach, befriended rulers and writers and escaped from prison. A richly anecdotal portrait of a far stranger intellectual and adventurer than the legend suggests.
subject: Giacomo Casanova

title: At Her Globe-Spanning Nightclubs, This Black Entertainer Hosted a 'Who's Who' of the 20th Century
description: Meet the magnetic singer and nightclub proprietor whose rooms from Paris to Rome drew writers, royalty, stars and a century of extraordinary conversations.
subject: Bricktop
